claim: An IMDA (Infocomm Media Development Authority) 2024 survey reportedly found that about 8% of Singaporeans aged 18-35 identify content creation as either their primary income source or their career goal.
stance_target: prevalence of content creation as a stated occupation/income source among young Singaporeans
scope_conditions: Singapore; ages 18-35; year 2024; UNCONFIRMED - statistic recoverable only from Google search-result snippets of a paywalled Campaign Asia/Campaign US article, not from the article's full text, and the original IMDA report/publication itself could not be located or fetched (IMDA's public Survey Reports and Research & Statistics pages did not surface a direct link in search).
quoted_support: According to a 2024 survey by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), around 8% of Singaporeans aged 18 to 35 identify content creation as either their primary income source or career goal.

claim: Singaporean content creators commonly earn between S$2,500 and S$6,000 per month, comparable to a fresh graduate's starting salary, and typically lack CPF contributions, paid leave, or employer-sponsored health insurance.
stance_target: content creation as a precarious/entry-level-equivalent income stream in Singapore, lacking standard employment benefits
scope_conditions: Singapore; UNCONFIRMED beyond search-snippet level - the underlying Campaign Asia/Campaign US article was paywalled and its full text (including sourcing/methodology for this income range) could not be retrieved.
quoted_support: A common experience involves creators earning enough to scrape by-typically between S$2,500 and S$6,000 per month, roughly equivalent to a fresh graduate's starting pay.
